root_cause: Progress.start() is guarded by `if not self.disable`, but Progress.stop() was not: it always called self.live.stop() and, on a non-interactive, non-Jupyter console, unconditionally ran self.console.print(), writing a stray '\n' even when Progress(disable=True).
best_solution: Mirror the guard in start(): wrap the whole body of Progress.stop() in `if not self.disable:` so both live.stop() and the trailing console.print() for non-interactive consoles are skipped when the display is disabled. A disabled Progress then writes nothing to the console file. The PR description states this exactly ('adds an if not self.disable to the stop function, symmetrically to the start function').
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_progress.py::test_no_output_if_progress_is_disabled_non_interactive: Console(file=StringIO(), force_interactive=False, width=60, color_system='truecolor', legacy_windows=False, _environ={}), Progress(console=console, disable=True), iterate progress.track(['foo','bar','baz']) inside `with progress:`; asserts console.file.getvalue() == '' (no blank line). Either guarding only the print() or the whole stop() body passes.
locating_signals: Statement names progress.py, the `disable` flag, the `stop` function, and 'symmetrically to the start function'; the gold function (Progress.stop) is named directly.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8) passed in the Kaggle env. v4/v6/v7 produced a patch byte-identical to gold (guard the whole stop() body); v8 guarded only the console.print() condition (`if not self.disable and not self.console.is_interactive ...`), leaving live.stop() unconditional, which still passes because Live.stop() is a no-op when never started. Pod runs 36-58 s, 16-27 calls.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement says a fix should be 'symmetric' to another method (start/stop, open/close, enter/exit, setup/teardown), open the sibling method, copy its guard condition verbatim into the counterpart, and wrap every side effect (including output writes) under it; then check the non-interactive/non-TTY branch, since output tests typically capture into a StringIO with force_interactive=False.
acceptable_alternatives: Guarding only the trailing console.print() with `not self.disable` (v8's patch) also passes, since Live.stop() on a never-started Live does nothing; gold guards the whole body for symmetry with start().
